_activity: Build the scene: the Monroe Doctrine, 1823
intro: Build the sentence. Drag the correct piece into each blank.

tiles.text: the War of 1812 ended with no land changing hands
Americans came out of the war proud, and nationalism was rising
colonists were still loyal to Britain
the embargo had crippled New England's shipping
1823, President Monroe told Europe to stay out of the Western Hemisphere
1825, the Erie Canal linked the Great Lakes to New York City

correct_sentence: After the War of 1812 ended with no land changing hands, Americans came out of the war proud, and nationalism was rising. By 1823, President Monroe told Europe to stay out of the Western Hemisphere.
rationale: The war is the 'after'. The pride it left behind is what was going on. The Doctrine is the 'by [year]'. Every wrong tile is a real fact from the same Day 1 page - wrong only about which slot it fills.
hints: Start with the war that ended in 1815.
'Nationalism' is one of your Day 1 vocabulary words.
